author: Jeff Lupien
releaseNotes:
v1.1.1: Fix key fetch - the Socket.IO state machine used atomicState.sio, which does not exist in drivers (app-only), so the fetch stalled silently after "Connecting..."; now state.sio. Callback/watchdog also log when they fire with no active fetch instead of returning silently.

v1.1.0: Local LAN control (hybrid) - per-unit device-key fetch (legacy v2 login + Socket.IO/Engine.IO polling session, ported from evdev/mitsubishi-comfort-hubitat), SHA-256 local auth token, sync local PUT for status + commands with cloud fallback, localKeyStatus attribute on the parent, connectionPath on each child, per-zone LAN IP preference + setUnitLanIp/clearUnitLanIp commands. Cloud behavior unchanged. Note: Mitsubishi stopped publishing local device keys for US Comfort-native accounts around Aug/Sep 2026, so the fetch may report "not published by cloud" - cloud control keeps working either way.

v1.0.4: Send units with temperature (°F) and humidity (%) events — dashboard tiles showed a bare number with no unit.

v1.0.3: cToF fallback rounds to a whole degree (heating setpoints below the table showed 50.9 instead of 51); accepted commands now log at info level.

v1.0.2: Replace the stale-status guard with a 90-second post-command suppression window — the lastStatusChangeAt comparison blocked settings updates forever after any command.

v1.0.1: Fix temperature table lookups in the child driver — Math.round() results are now cast to int so the Fahrenheit/Celsius lookup tables actually match (cooling setpoint showed 67.1 instead of 67).

v1.0.0: Initial release - Comfort app (Kumo Cloud v3 API) support for Mitsubishi mini-splits. JWT login + token refresh, site/zone discovery with automatic child device creation, scheduled polling, and thermostat control (mode, setpoints, fan speed, vane) via POST /v3/devices/send-command. Replaces the Kumo Cloud half of the Unified Thermostat driver, whose v2 API died in the March 2025 Comfort migration.
